I made one structural change in `transcribe/engines/faster_whisper.py`, marked one real bug without fixing it, and left the other hotspots alone. Test results before and after are identical; nothing is committed.

## A bug I found and did not fix

`split_cues(..., return_words=True)` returns `[]` instead of `([], [])` when it gets no words. `faster_whisper.transcribe` unpacks two values from it, so a decode that finds no speech (for example a silent file) crashes with `ValueError`. This is the cause of the existing red test `test_transcribe_threads_speech_spans`.

Fixing it would change behavior, so I only marked it with an `untangle: known bug:` comment at both places it happens: `transcribe/cues/split.py:177` and `transcribe/cues/split.py:416`. The fix is to return `([], [])` there when `return_words` is true.

## What I changed and why

**`transcribe/engines/faster_whisper.py`.** This file has had the most fixes (16 of its 31 commits), and most of them landed in the code that re-decodes audio Whisper dropped at the end of a window. That code existed in three copies:
- The fix for issue #73 (don't pass `initial_prompt`/`hotwords` into these retries) had to be written twice, which is why two separate tests check it.
- The step that shifts the new words into window time and joins them to the kept words was copied three times.

Now:
- `_tail_decode_kwargs()` is the one place the retry settings are built.
- `_splice_tail()` is the one place the shift-and-join happens.
- `_recover_truncated_tail` now calls the single-window branch of `_batch_recover_tails` instead of repeating it. Its log line is unchanged.

The next fix to this logic lands in one place instead of two or three.

**New guard test, `tests/test_faster_whisper_tail_seam.py`.** It checks that every retry path goes through those two helpers, plus the shift-and-join results. It passes on the new code and fails on the old, so it will catch the copies coming back.

## What I left alone

- **`uxp/cutdeck/main.js`:** already split up by an earlier refactor; it now only connects the features together.
- **`timeline/nativeCut.js`:** the repeated fixes for Premiere handles going stale mid-batch are already in one shared path.
- **`features/align.js` and `timeline/adjustmentLayer.js`:** each fix is a different live Premiere finding, not the same fault repeating. Reworking them is only safe with a live Premiere run, and I had none.
- **`db/store.py`:** CLAUDE.md requires it to be the only file with raw SQL, so changes landing there is by design.
- **`eval/harness.py`:** the regression-gate logic was already moved out to `eval/gate.py`.
- **`core/panel.js` and the files that change together:** these are wiring and view/logic pairs that are meant to change together.

Each skipped file that had many fixes has a named test command that still passes. The reasons for every decision are in `.untangle/notes.md`.

## How I know nothing broke

I ran both full suites on the committed code first, then again after the change:

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `node --test tests/*.cjs` | 731 tests, 0 failing | 731, 0 failing |
| `pytest tests` | 1151 tests, 10 failing | 1154 (3 new guard tests), the same 10 failing |

None of the 10 failures came from this change:
- **8 in `test_text_box.py`:** an environment problem. `uharfbuzz` is in `requirements.txt` but not installed here.
- **1, `test_cue_knobs_reach_the_splitter`:** the test is out of date. Its fake `split_cues` was never updated to accept `return_words` when that argument was added.
- **1, `test_transcribe_threads_speech_spans`:** the bug above.

The untangle skill's final check passed (`UNTANGLE-GATE: done`). It confirmed that no passing test turned red and no suite ran fewer tests. Nothing here was checked against a GPU or a live Premiere.

Both modified files, the new test and `.untangle/` are uncommitted on `master`. Commit `.untangle/` with the change or delete it.
